newsitem.title: USA: CIGNA Q1 up, helped by health, property.
newsitem.headline: CIGNA Q1 up, helped by health, property.

text.p: CIGNA Corp's first-quarter profits topped Wall Street's consensus estimate by about 13 percent, helped by better-than-expected health care results and gains in the property-casualty business.
"I think the news in the quarter is that the health care margins seem to be bottoming," Sanford C. Bernstein analyst Weston Hicks said. He also cited an improvement in the medical loss ratio.
CIGNA reported first quarter operating earnings of $3.49 a share compared with the First Call consensus of $3.11 a share.
CIGNA said its ongoing property-casualty and individual financial services businesses also contributed to the strong performance.
First quarter operating income for the ongoing property-casualty operations rose to $56 million from $41 million a year ago, CIGNA said.
The first quarter combined ratio was 100 percent compared with 105 percent a year ago.
After-tax catastrophe losses fell to $8 million in the first quarter compared with $15 million a year ago.
The international property-casualty operations had first quarter operating income $33 million, up from $29 million a year ago.
The domestic property-casualty business had first quarter operating income of $23 million compared with $12 million in 1996.
Hicks said CIGNA continues to downsize its domestic property-casualty business in favor of expanding outside of the United States.
"There's a tremendous mix shift going on underneath these numbers," he said.
CIGNA said its run-off operations had operating income of $1 million in the first quarter of 1997 and 1996.
In the individual financial services segment, first-quarter operating income rose to $47 million from $32 million a year ago.
This segment includes individual and corporate life insurance; life, accident and health reinsurance; and annuity businesses.
HMO earnings were $59 million in the first quarter compared with $56 million a year ago.
HMO medical membership grew by approximately 275,000 covered lives, or 7%, since March 31, 1996.
